name: The Judas Factor
label: Revelation
lede: Rob Fish's band after Ressurection went through its first guitarist in three shows, swung from brutal to soft indie mid-record, and counts a future New York City councilman among its early members.

eras.title: Five practices and a 7"
eras.text: After Ressurection, singer Rob Fish put a new band together from friends in Indecision and Ressurection's old bassist. They barely rehearsed before recording, and the first line-up didn't last the year.

years.h: Rob Fish forms The Judas Factor with two from Indecision
years.p: Rob Fish recruits Pat and [[Justin Brannan|2cf0dcde-8417-46ff-96a9-74328669b417]] from Indecision, Ressurection's bassist Little Dave, and his old Ressurection guitarist [[Chris Zusi|2a9965ad-0a98-4665-9bc0-aebec823fb44]]. Zusi says they practiced five to eight times before recording.
The Judas Factor's first record, on Wreck-Age, with Chris Zusi on guitar.

years.h: Chris Zusi fired after two or three shows; Brannan soon out
years.p: Chris Zusi played The Judas Factor's first two or three shows and was let go. Justin Brannan and Pat were out soon after, and the band went in a different direction.
years.xp: Zusi had played with Rob Fish in Ressurection from 1991 to 1995, and went on to [[Floorpunch|8ecf80c2-d090-4cbd-97ec-0a0824301041]]. He says Fish had a definite idea of where he wanted the new band to go.

eras.title: The Victorian bathtub years
eras.text: On Revelation, The Judas Factor made two albums that broke from the chug of late-'90s hardcore, with song titles that read like short stories.

years.p: It opens on brutal riffs, turns into soft indie rock midway, then goes heavy again. Twelve songs, including That Beautiful Old Victorian Bathtub; the first vinyl pressing is 169 on red.
The Judas Factor's second Revelation album. The only vinyl pressing is 223 copies on opaque green.

eras.title: From Indecision to City Hall
eras.text: One of the original Judas Factor members ended up in New York City government.

years.src: Wikipedia: Justin Brannan · No Echo · Discogs
years.h: Ex-Judas Factor guitarist Justin Brannan joins the NYC Council
years.p: Justin Brannan, of Indecision, [[Most Precious Blood|1f43313f-4855-4b5f-af16-90ab6ab8cf36]] and briefly The Judas Factor, takes his seat for Brooklyn's 43rd district. In 2025 he runs for city comptroller and finishes second in the Democratic primary.
years.xp: Brannan served on the Council from 2018 through 2025, moving to the 47th district in 2024. In the 2025 comptroller primary he took 41.28% in the final round to Mark Levine's 58.72%.
